correctness.rationale: Every T_i is strictly increasing, positive and below x because T_i’=1-u_i K_i/(K_i+x)^2>0. Exact common-denominator expansion gives T_j(T_i(x))-T_i(T_j(x))=-uv x² P(x)/D(x), D>0, P(x)=(K-L)x²+[(K-L)(K+L)-Ku+Lv]x+KL(K-L-u+v). For K>L, if K-u>=L-v, all P coefficients nonnegative and at least leading and linear strictly positive, so larger-K-first wins at every x>0. If K-u<L-v, the leading coefficient is positive, constant negative, and the quadratic has exactly one positive zero x*, so preference reverses there. A finite family has finitely many switches; low-x inputs and all intermediate stage inputs are below them, whereas for high-x, all intermediate inputs remain >x-sum(u_i), above the switches. Strict adjacent interchanges improve any inverted pair under those ranges, producing unique optimal total orders, and their difference rules out any universal order. Independently reduced symbolic commutator to zero and verified exact rational example P=(x-1)(x+5/6) with switch x=1.

value.rationale: A complete robust universal ordering test (and precise failure mechanism) is a natural optimization question for multiple saturable finite-step removal stages. It replaces parameter-dependent brute-force permutation searches with a two-index criterion while sharply explaining concentration-induced reversals. A reusable exact result in a motivated discrete environmental processing model, not a claim of field validation.
residual_risks: Practical streams violate the highly restricted constant-flow one-pass assumptions; significance is mathematical model classification rather than environmental policy prediction.

final_claim: For distinct K_i and 0<u_i<K_i, maps T_i(x)=x-u_i*x/(K_i+x) have an all-x globally minimizing order iff K_i>K_j implies K_i-u_i>=K_j-u_j for every pair. The unique universal order then sorts decreasing K. At sufficiently small inputs the unique optimum sorts decreasing (K-u,K) lexicographically, and at large inputs decreasing K. Any reversed residual pair switches its two-stage preference exactly once at a quadratic root.
